steps.question: How dense is the layout?
steps.why: Room around the text helps reading.
Text needs air even inside a group.

steps.question: What separates groups on the page?
steps.why: Space separates groups; lines would interrupt reading.

steps.rule: The edge of a control people must find.
steps.pick: neutral.500: the edge of a control people must find, 4.86:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.400: the edge of a control people must find, 6.16:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.question: How dense is the layout?
steps.why: Room around the text helps reading.

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A lead and a display role open articles.
Rounded corners match the warm reading tone. Sharp corners feel technical next to long text.
Caption is too faint for a label people must read.

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
steps.pick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.12:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
steps.darkPick: neutral.floor: We use the floor step, below the page's canvas, for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.16:1 under content and 1.06:1 under the canvas. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.rule: Quiet edges and dividers. Decorative, so it has no contrast minimum.
steps.pick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.33:1, on surface.canvas). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: a quiet line that stays visible on every surface it meets (lowest 1.46:1, on surface.raised). It decorates, so it holds no contrast minimum.

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a warm tone, by brand convention. A rounded radius does this by curving the edge enough to feel soft, while the sides stay straight. So controls feel friendly next to long text and never compete with it, because the brand is warm (brand.q1), corners are rounded (shape.values) and each screen holds one idea (content.q2).
